references.text: The priests were rebuked for not eating the sin offering in a holy place, which shows the seriousness of handling holy gifts correctly.
Whoever eats the peace offering improperly bears their guilt because they have profaned what is holy to the Lord.
The priests must keep the Lord's regulations so as not to incur sin and die by profaning the holy things.
The context concerns guilt incurred by eating holy gifts in error, and that the priests must not allow the people to profane the holy gifts.
Warning against incurring sin by profaning the Israelites' holy gifts.
The Lord declares, 'I am the Lord who sanctifies you' - the same expression confirming God's role as the one who makes holy.
The Lord sanctifies the priests, making the same theological point about God's role as the one who makes holy.
The priests are to teach the people the difference between holy and common, clean and unclean.
